#!/bin/bash
#FLUX --job-name=SWE_otfTraining
#FLUX --output={name}.o{id}
#FLUX --error={name}.e{id}
#FLUX --nodes=1
#FLUX --tasks-per-node=1
#FLUX --gpus=1
#FLUX --queue=gpu
#FLUX --mem=32G
#FLUX --time=12:00:00

# al piu' 128gb di ram per gpu in media
# con il comando 'seff' controllo efficienza memoria
# --gres=gpu:1

module load miniconda3
source "$CONDA_PREFIX/etc/profile.d/conda.sh" 
conda activate swe-cv-pytorch

cd ..
python -u train_otf_grid.py -root ../datasets/arda/ -epochs 500 -image_size 768 -out_channels 3 -buffer_size 100 -buffer_memory 100

issues: The job requests a GPU but does not explicitly request any CPU resources via `--cpus-per-task`. Flux will likely default to allocating a single CPU core. This can create a significant performance bottleneck, as the CPU may be unable to keep the GPU fed with data, leading to underutilization of the expensive GPU resource. It is recommended to explicitly request a reasonable number of CPUs (e.g., `--cpus-per-task=8`) to support the GPU workload.

The command `cd ..` is executed before the main Python script. The success of the script depends on the job's initial working directory being a specific subdirectory of the project. If the job is submitted from an unexpected location, this relative path change will place the execution in the wrong directory, likely causing the subsequent `python` command to fail with a 'file not found' error when trying to access `../datasets/arda/`. Using absolute paths or changing to a known project root directory is more robust.
